title: feat(types): a DataSource record id is a string on delete and the bulk pair (objectui#9511)
body:
Part of #9511 — this branch lands the part of the ruling that measured clean and
carries the rest back to the card. ⛔ It does **not** complete the card: one of
the five doors is still open by measurement, so there is no closing keyword in
this body on purpose.

Clause-②: yes

Executing director batch #136 item 5, letter **B** (maintainer 「同意」
2026-09-15T15:20Z): a record id at the `DataSource` boundary is a string.
objectui#9333 narrowed `update`; this branch narrows three more doors.

## What landed

| declaration | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `DataSource.delete` — `id` | string OR number | **string** |
| `DataSource.bulkUpdate` — `ids` | ReadonlyArray OF (string OR number) | **ReadonlyArray OF string** |
| `DataSource.bulkDelete` — `ids` | ReadonlyArray OF (string OR number) | **ReadonlyArray OF string** |
| `UseViewDataResult.fetchOne` — `id` (`@object-ui/react`) | string OR number | **string** |

⚠️ The type spellings in that table are written as WORDS (`OR`, `ReadonlyArray
OF`). GitHub's body sanitizer eats tag-shaped fragments even inside backticks,
and it has previously collapsed both columns of exactly this kind of
before/after table into the same string.

Plus the thing the ruling's acceptance asks for: the `DataSource` docblock now
states the rule once, for the whole interface, including why the last door is
still open — so the next reader does not rediscover the asymmetry.

The three one-layer-in declarations the ruling names (`TransactionOperation.id`,
`UserPreferenceRecord.id`, `resolveRecordId`'s return) were **already narrowed**
by the merged objectui#9501; verified by symbol on this tree. `fetchOne` is the
one the compiler added to that list.

## What did not land, and why

⚠️ **This section was re-derived after the at-tier review failed its first
version.** The earlier text said `findOne`'s remaining readers resolve to two
authorable metadata keys, with six of them in `@object-ui/plugin-form`. That was
false, and it shipped in the docblock and the changeset as well as here. What
follows is re-measured on this branch; the docblock and the changeset now carry
the same corrected reading.

`DataSource.findOne` keeps `string OR number`. The compiler enumerated nine
in-tree call sites for it; one was `fetchOne` (narrowed here), and the other
eight split two ways.

**Three read AUTHORABLE metadata keys.** `ObjectForm.tsx` reads
`ObjectFormSchema.recordId` (`packages/types/src/objectql.ts` + its zod mirror);
`DetailView.tsx` reads `DetailViewSchema.resourceId` at two sites
(`packages/types/src/views.ts` + `zod/views.zod.ts`). ⚠️ A sibling declaration of
the same key, `DetailSchema.resourceId`, lives in `crud.ts` + `zod/crud.zod.ts`
and is **not** read by either red site — four declaration sites of `resourceId`
across four files, owned by two symbols. Measured against the BUILT mirrors,
with a lit control in the same pass:

```
ObjectFormSchema.safeParse({type:'object-form', objectName:'accounts', mode:'edit', recordId: 42})
  -> success = TRUE, and the parsed document KEEPS 42 as a number
ObjectFormSchema.safeParse({… recordId: '42'})            -> TRUE
LIT CONTROL  ObjectFormSchema.safeParse({… recordId: {}}) -> FALSE (invalid_union)
DetailViewSchema.safeParse({type:'detail-view', objectName:'accounts', resourceId: 42})
  -> TRUE
LIT CONTROL  DetailViewSchema.safeParse({… resourceId: {}}) -> FALSE (invalid_union)
```

**Five read a `recordId` on their OWN exported schema face** — `DrawerForm`,
`ModalForm`, `SplitForm`, `TabbedForm`, `WizardForm`, each declaring its own
`FormSchema` interface in its own file and exporting it from
`packages/plugin-form/src/index.tsx`. Those faces are TypeScript-only, i.e. the
same class as `UseViewDataResult.fetchOne`, which this PR narrows:

| instrument | the five | lit control | corpus |
|---|---|---|---|
| occurrences in the zod mirror tree | 0 each | `ObjectFormSchema` = 5 | `packages/types/src/zod/` |
| node-type string literal outside tests | 0 each | `'object-form'` = 34 | `packages/*/src`, `apps/*/src` |

Both instruments fire on the control, so those zeros are readings rather than
dead queries.

**They still cannot narrow ahead of the decision, and that is measured too.**
`ObjectForm` BUILDS all five of those schemas from its own authorable
`ObjectFormSchema`. Narrowing the five alone was probed on this branch: the five
declarations were rewritten to `string` (landing proven on disk — five files
injected, zero left wide), the packages rebuilt, and `ObjectForm.tsx` answered
`TS2322` at five hand-off sites, one per delegated form, each reading
`Types of property 'recordId' are incompatible`. The probe was restored with
`git checkout HEAD --` and an empty `git status` proves it.

⇒ closing `findOne` means either **narrowing a published authoring face** (author
JSON that validates today stops validating — an accept-set change the ruling does
not name) or **converting at a reader** (which the ruling's own "the conversion
lives in one typed place" argues against). Both are decisions, not
implementations, so they are carried to the card rather than picked here — and
the five TypeScript-only faces travel with that decision instead of ahead of it.

Second, independent block on the authorable half: `packages/types/src/objectql.ts`
and `packages/types/src/zod/objectql.zod.ts` are the declared file surface of
in-flight card objectui#9606. The dispatch order for this card says to stop and
report rather than edit them, so this card yields on that half.

## Measurements

Every exit code was captured to disk before any pipe.

| gate | exit | printed verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `turbo run build type-check --filter='!@object-ui/site' --concurrency=2 --continue` | 0 | `Tasks: 88 successful, 88 total` |
| `examples/byo-backend-console` → `pnpm run type-check` | 0 | `tsc --noEmit`, no diagnostics |
| `@object-ui/core` → `pnpm run type-check` | 0 | `tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`, no diagnostics |
| `vitest run packages/types/ packages/react/` | 0 | `Test Files 290 passed (290)` · `Tests 5778 passed (5778)` |
| `vitest run packages/data-objectstack/` + the two bulk-path files | 0 | `Test Files 68 passed (68)` · `Tests 918 passed (918)` |
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/types --filter @object-ui/react run lint` | 0 | `362 problems (0 errors, 362 warnings)` — all pre-existing |
| `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` | 0 | 3 source files of 2 released packages, 1 changeset declared |
| `node scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` | 0 | `No changeset declares a major bump.` |
| `node scripts/check-changeset-fixed.mjs` | 0 | `All workspace packages are in the changeset fixed group.` |
| `node scripts/check-new-cross-file-line-citations.mjs` | 0 | `0 new citation(s)` |
| `node scripts/check-control-bytes.mjs` | 0 | scanned 7813 tracked text files |

### The opposite-answer probe, per door

A temporary probe under `packages/types/src/__tests__/` (removed before the first
commit) called each door with a numeric id and was compiled by
`tsc -p packages/types/tsconfig.test.json`:

- **before** the narrowing: exit **0** — all four numeric calls accepted.
  ⭐ Lit control in the same file and the same run: `update`, already narrow on
  `main`, produced exactly one `TS2345`. So the instrument reports numeric-id
  refusals; the four zeros were absence, not a dead query.
- **after** the narrowing: exit **2** — `findOne` `TS2345`, `delete` `TS2345`,
  `bulkUpdate` `TS2322`, `bulkDelete` `TS2322`, while the four string calls beside
  them stayed legal.

### Ablation of the new pin

`packages/types/src/__tests__/data-source-id-surface-9511.test.ts` was ablated by
widening `delete`'s `id` back, from a committed tree:

- mutation proven on disk: injected spelling present (1), byte size 53257 → 53266,
  blob `805d1269` → `619d0d9a`
- ablated `vitest`: exit **1** — `Tests 1 failed | 8 passed`, message
  `DataSource.delete declares a record id wider than the protocol.`
- ablated `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`: exit **1** — `TS2344` on the `Equal` row and
  `TS2578` (unused directive) on the `@ts-expect-error` call-site control, i.e.
  both designed failure modes
- restored with `git checkout HEAD -- packages/types/src/data.ts`; restoration
  proven by blob equality (`805d1269` both sides) and an empty `git diff HEAD`

### Probe: can the five TypeScript-only form faces narrow on their own?

No, and the answer is a build, not an argument. The five `recordId` declarations
were rewritten to `string`; the mutation was proven on disk (five files carrying
the injected spelling, zero left wide) before anything was read. `plugin-form`
then failed to build with `TS2322` at five `ObjectForm.tsx` hand-off sites —
`ObjectForm` constructs each delegated schema from its own authorable
`ObjectFormSchema`. (`plugin-designer`'s failures in the same run are cascade:
`TS7016`, no `plugin-form` dist.) Restored with `git checkout HEAD --`, proven
by an empty `git status`.

### Cost attribution, per door

With `findOne` alone widened back and the other three doors narrowed, the whole
repo builds: `Tasks: 43 successful, 43 total`, exit 0. ⇒ `delete`, `bulkUpdate`
and `bulkDelete` have **zero** call sites in this monorepo that had to change;
the entire call-site cost of this card belongs to `findOne`.

## Acceptance notes

- The ruling cites `data.ts` at three line addresses; all five members were
  located **by symbol** instead, and no line address was written into any
  published text here.
- Noted, not filed: `data.ts` carries an **orphaned** docblock — the
  "Universal data source interface" comment sits about seventy lines above
  `export interface DataSource`, immediately before the `GlobalSearchHit`
  comment, so `DataSource` itself had no attached doc at all. That is why the
  rule went into a **new** block attached to the interface rather than into that
  one. Left in place deliberately: moving it is a different defect class from
  this card's, and no in-flight PR or reader is blocked by it. Successor: none
  identified.

## Review posture

⛔ Draft, ⛔ not enqueued, ⛔ no auto-merge — the PM runs an at-tier contract
review first. `needs:contract-review` is hung on this PR as well as on the card.
